title: quarantine-registry.ts: 8 entries cite closed issues (#1652, #2997, #3219) — stale references
body:
## What's stale

`scripts/quarantine-registry.live.test.ts` (excluded from CI — no `gh` auth there, per its own file, but runnable locally with auth) asserts every entry's `issue` field points at something OPEN. Running it locally today (2026-08-19, as part of #3497's nightly triage) surfaces 3 closed issues still cited by 8 entries:

| Issue | Status | Cited by |
|---|---|---|
| #1652 | CLOSED 2026-08-19 | `LAYOUT_ROUTE_QUARANTINE` (4 entries: `dashboard/portfolio`, `dashboard/board/:boardId/details/board-package-preview`, `dashboard/board/:boardId/investors-research`, `dashboard/board/:boardId/team/members`), `L4_RECIPE_VIEWPORT_QUARANTINE` (1 entry: voting-slots@tablet-768) |
| #2997 | CLOSED 2026-08-12 | `L4_ROUTE_QUARANTINE` (3 entries: `dashboard/portfolio`, `dashboard/board/:boardId/bets`, `dashboard/board/:boardId/knowledge-graph/guided-interview`) |
| #3219 | CLOSED 2026-08-12 | `STATE_RECIPES_WALKER_QUARANTINE` (1 entry, `active: false`, reporting-only: `state-recipes-meetings-overlay-walker@mobile-pixel5`) |

## Per-entry disposition (read each issue's close-out before touching)

**#1652's close-out** explicitly scoped itself to `QUARANTINED #1642` markers (S3/recipe repair work) and named `MOBILE_LAYOUT_GATE_QUARANTINE`/`L4_ROUTE_QUARANTINE` as deliberately excluded (owned by #3343/#3111) — but did **not** address the 5 entries above, which is why they're now orphaned rather than resolved. These 5 findings' current status is unverified — needs re-measurement against current `main`, then either a fresh tracking issue or removal if fixed incidentally.

**#2997's close-out** ("Re-measured — stable. Recommending close.") resolved the tablet-768 width-nondeterminism the issue was filed around, but explicitly separated out the L4_ROUTE_QUARANTINE height-drift findings (portfolio/bets/kg-guided-interview — chart-heavy routes, async content not settling before screenshot) as "a different, still-live finding" rolling up to #3102 for a baseline-regeneration decision. #3102 is also now closed (successor is #3497, but #3497 is the broader nightly-CI-health tracker, not a natural home for 3 specific route findings). These 3 entries need a fresh, narrowly-scoped issue.

**#3219's close-out** reports the `mobile-pixel5` meetings-list Notifications-popover-overlap finding this specific entry cites as **fixed** (`NotificationBell`'s Popover anchoring + responsive panel width, verified visually before/after). Corroborating: nightly run 32305107279 (2026-08-19, current `main`) shows **no** mobile-pixel5 state-recipes overlay-walker failure — but **does** show a new one: `mobile-iphone13` › `L3: Overlay walker` › `dashboard: every overlay renders without layout bugs` › `dashboard overlay (popover-trigger): Notifications` (1 finding). Same bug shape (Notifications popover), different device/route — likely the fix didn't fully generalize, or this is a fresh recurrence. This entry should be **removed** (finding resolved) and a **new** entry added for the mobile-iphone13/dashboard recurrence.

## Suggested next step

Not attempted here as live code changes — filed as part of #3497's nightly-CI-health triage, which is scoped to getting the nightly suites to a decided state, not a full re-investigation of every orphaned registry entry. Whoever picks this up should re-measure each of the 8 findings against current `main` (per the registry's own culture: "an unquarantined deterministic failure is an unfiled finding," and equally, a fixed one shouldn't stay quarantined) before deciding fresh-issue vs. removal per entry.

## Provenance

`npx vitest run scripts/quarantine-registry.live.test.ts` run locally 2026-08-19 (with `gh` auth) against `main` @ 8da2721e + the two safe fixes from #3497's session (sign-in locator, pages snapshot regen) — first assertion failure was `#1652 is CLOSED, not OPEN`; the other 7 stale citations found by manually checking `gh issue view` for every `issue:` field in the registry.

title: test(e2e): unregistered-member factory has no real-UI write test — the "Add unregistered" dialog is a real creation form
body:
## Provenance

Filed from #3746's review. `packages/frontend/tests/factories/board-user-unregistered.factory.ts` was added there to seed a `MAX_UNREGISTERED_DISPLAY_NAME_LENGTH` member for the boundary-value recipes.

## The gap

`docs/qa/e2e-testing-guide.md`'s Required Real-UI Coverage rule (#2976) says a new factory must have at least one real-UI test for the same entity, and that an entity may be exempted only when it **cannot** be tested through the real form. Unregistered members *can*: the "Add unregistered" dialog on `dashboard/board/:boardId/team/members` is a real creation form.

So this is a **gap**, not an exemption. #3746 recorded it as such — a row in the guide's coverage table (`None yet — gap`) and a `#2976` opt-out annotation in the factory header — rather than claiming an exemption it isn't entitled to.

Why it wasn't closed in #3746: that issue made the dialog *reachable* by the L3 overlay walker (the walker now opens it and asserts layout inside it). Opening a dialog is not filling it in. A real-UI write spec is its own piece of work and would have been an unrelated rider on a test-infrastructure change.

## What it would take

A Playwright spec on the members route that opens the "Add unregistered" dialog through the real UI, submits a display name, and asserts the row appears — the same shape as `tests/team-management.spec.ts`'s "G-2: Invite New Member". The factory's payload (`POST /api/v1/boards/:boardId/unregistered-members`, `{ displayName }`) can then be checked against what the dialog actually sends, which is the divergence class #2976 exists to catch.

## Done when

- [ ] A real-UI write test creates an unregistered member through the dialog.
- [ ] `docs/qa/e2e-testing-guide.md`'s row for Unregistered Member moves from `None yet — gap` to that test.
- [ ] The `#2976` opt-out annotation is removed from `tests/factories/board-user-unregistered.factory.ts`.

title: chore(testing): triage 8 quarantine entries older than 14 days (4 at 84 days) per the tier model
body:
Surfaced by the 2026-08-28 nightly RCA (#3880) and parked there as out of scope.

## What's wrong

8 entries in the quarantine registry are older than 14 days; 4 of them are at 84 days. Per the E2E tier model (\`docs/qa/e2e-testing-guide.md\` → "The E2E Tier Model", #3103/#3111), a quarantine entry is either a \`finding\`/\`backlog\` (a real bug or parked epic — needs an issue, no timer) or a \`flake\` (a falsifiable, measured-temporary claim). An entry sitting 84 days with no disposition is neither — it's unowned.

This is the **age** axis of registry rot; the sibling issue #3631 covers the **stale-citation** axis (8 entries citing closed issues). Some entries may appear in both sets — triage should join them.

## What should happen

For each of the 8 aged entries:

- [ ] Confirm current status against \`main\` (still failing? fixed incidentally?)
- [ ] Disposition per the tier model: real bug → file/link an issue and mark \`finding\`; genuinely temporary → keep \`flake\` with fresh window evidence; fixed → remove the entry
- [ ] Entries citing closed issues get the #3631 treatment in the same pass (or are explicitly handed to it)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Zero quarantine entries older than 14 days without a current disposition (or a documented reason the age rule doesn't apply)
- [ ] The disposition list is posted on this issue before closing

Refs: #3880 (RCA), #3631 (stale citations), #3111 (registry vocabulary), #3497 (nightly CI health)

title: fix(fue): notification-bell tour step copy is vague — "Your board talks to you here."
body:
## Where

`main/packages/frontend/src/components/onboarding/tours/tour-definitions.ts` (`boardIntroTour`, step 2 of 4) — the mandatory first-run tour every new/demo user hits after signup (`allowClose:false`, no skip/dismiss).

```ts
{
  element: '[data-tour="notification-bell"]',
  popover: {
    title: 'Notifications',
    description: 'Your board talks to you here.',
    side: 'bottom',
    align: 'center',
  },
},
```

## Problem

The description doesn't say what a notification actually is or why the user would check it — "your board talks to you" is a slogan, not information. It's step 2 of a mandatory onboarding tour every new user is forced through, so this is the app's introduction to a core surface, wasted.

## What notifications actually contain

Per `packages/shared-types/src/types/notification.types.ts` (`NotificationTypes`): board invites/membership changes, board activity (new comments, task assignment), meeting updates (slot proposals, RSVP changes, cancellations, post-meeting minutes), and dashboard/report status (assigned, ready for review, published).

## Suggested fix

Swap the description for something that actually conveys content, in the same terse register as the other 3 steps in this tour ("Stuck? Everything starts here." / "Move around your board from here." / "Your account and settings."):

> "Invites, comments, and meeting updates land here."

(Title `Notifications` is fine as-is — it matches the plain-noun naming style the other steps use.)

## Note

`tests/guide-review` (the tour-audit harness, epic #3645) has this exact string baked into its baseline manifest (`tests/guide-review/baselines/replayIntroTour/seeded-board.manifest.json`) as the *expected* value — see #3841 for why the harness never flags copy like this. Whoever fixes this must regenerate that baseline in the same PR (`pnpm guide:review replayIntroTour --update-baselines`, run twice, second run zero-diff — per the harness's own dossier at `docs/dossiers/guide-review.ds.md`).

title: test(flake-telemetry): #3886 follow-ups — e2e-advisory-report still keys on spec:line, flatten copy-pasted 4x, traps row blocked on capacity
body:
Surfaced by the review phase of #3886 (PR pending). #3886 fixed `scripts/flake-window.mjs` so its aggregation key ignores the spec's `:LINE`; these are the loose ends that review found but that were deliberately left out of that PR to keep it scoped.

## 1. `e2e-advisory-report.mjs` still keys on `spec:line` — the two window consumers now disagree

`main/scripts/e2e-advisory-report.mjs` is the *other* consumer of the same `.flake-window.json`, and it still builds its correlation key with the line number in it:

- `main/scripts/e2e-advisory-report.mjs:174` — `` const key = `${rec.spec}|${rec.title}|${rec.project}` `` (window side; `rec.spec` is `file:LINE`)
- `main/scripts/e2e-advisory-report.mjs:190` — `` const key = `${specId}|${title}|${project}` `` where `specId` is built as `` `${flatten(spec.file)}:${flatten(spec.line)}` ``

**Impact:** a PR that shifts line numbers earlier in a file it touches can make a genuinely pre-existing failure miss the correlation and get reported to the author as "possibly introduced" / "no nightly coverage" — the exact #3886 failure mode, on the PR-comment surface instead of the nightly-table surface. Two CI surfaces read one window file and now disagree about identity.

#3886's PR updates that script's `KNOWN LIMITATION` header comment so it no longer falsely claims key parity with the window, but does **not** change the behavior.

**Fix:** apply the same line-strip on both sides of the key (keep `specId` line-carrying for the *displayed* `line` string at `:191` — the display-vs-key split #3886 established). `scripts/tests/test-e2e-advisory-report.sh` (32 assertions) already has fixtures at lines 160/220/300 that make this verifiable. The user-facing text at `:245` ("a naming mismatch between this run's spec:line and the window's") needs updating too.

## 2. `flatten` is copy-pasted verbatim in four scripts

Byte-identical in all four, each with its own `eslint-disable-next-line no-control-regex` and its own comment pointing at the others:

- `scripts/flake-window.mjs`
- `scripts/parse-issue-citations.mjs`
- `main/scripts/playwright-summary.mjs`
- `main/scripts/e2e-advisory-report.mjs`

#3886 hardened this helper (added U+0085/U+2028/U+2029 to the stripped class, since Telegram renders U+2028 as a hard line break and would split a table row) in **one** copy only — so the four have now actually diverged, not just duplicated.

**Fix:** extract `flatten` + `stripLine` into `scripts/lib/text.mjs` and import from the two worktree-root scripts. Note `e2e-advisory-report.mjs:127-132` documents an explicit prior decision *not* to share helpers across the `main/` workspace boundary, so the two `main/scripts/` copies may need to stay separate or get their own shared module — worth deciding rather than assuming.

## 3. `agent-traps.md` row for the fossilized-key trap (blocked on capacity)

The trap generalizes well past this script: **any aggregation key built from a citation, `path+line`, or stack frame fossilizes on any line-shifting edit.** Symptom is distinctive and hard to diagnose — a rolling report insists a test fails 100% of the time while that test passes every night at its current line, the row never moves, and no re-run reproduces it.

Not added in #3886's PR because `main/docs/agent-traps.md` is at exactly its stated **~80-row capacity**, and the file's own rule requires promoting the oldest row to `AGENTS.md` (as its own `###` subsection) before appending — an unrelated conventions-file restructure that did not belong in a bugfix PR. #3886's mandatory trigger ("any CI-fix commit must add exactly one row") did not fire, since that PR needed no CI fixes.

**Fix:** promote the oldest row per the capacity rule, then append:

| Symptom | Trap | Fix | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| A nightly/rolling report row insists a test fails 100% of the time (e.g. `cross-cutting.spec.ts:342`) while that same test passes every night at its CURRENT line; the row never moves and no re-run reproduces it | An aggregation key that embeds a source LINE NUMBER (Playwright's `spec` is `file:LINE`) fossilizes: any unrelated line-shifting edit mints a brand-new key from the next run on, and the old key's records sit in the rolling window as a frozen row no future run can ever match again. Same shape hits any key built from a citation, `path+line`, or stack frame. | Key aggregation on line-STRIPPED identity (`stripLine()` in `scripts/flake-window.mjs`) and keep the line as a DISPLAY field only, reassigned last-write-wins so the row shows the current location. Shown-but-not-keyed is safe; keyed-but-not-shown is not. | #3886 (surfaced by #3880's RCA) |

## 4. Test-fixture helpers duplicated across the two flake-window suites

`record()` and `write_records_file()` are copy-pasted between `scripts/tests/test-flake-window.sh` and `scripts/tests/test-flake-window-status.sh` (they differ only in arity). #3886 improved the render suite's copy (jq-based, so a fixture value containing a quote or backslash can't silently emit malformed JSONL) — leaving the status suite's copy with the original footgun. Move both into `scripts/tests/lib/`, sibling to the existing `assert.sh` / `stub.sh` / `gh-issue-stub.sh`.

Refs: #3886, #3880 (RCA), #3110 (flake window), #3476 (citation matching), tracker #3126

title: test(e2e): residual walker findings on sidebar-adjacent chrome — tablet footer-span text-clip + mobile nav-Sheet overlap remnants
body:
Surfaced by #3885's conformance review (dispatched nightly [33211009019](https://example.invalid/redacted-run) vs baseline [33176296104](https://example.invalid/redacted-run), diffed line-by-line). After the sidebar-misattribution fix (#3878 trigger guard + #3885's \`[data-sidebar]\` exclusion on overflow/overlap), two pre-existing shapes remain, currently tracked nowhere:

1. **Sidebar-footer name/email span text-clip at tablet (768–1023).** The sidebar is force-collapsed to icon mode at that band by design (#3360), and the user-menu trigger's \`line-clamp-1\` spans (\`Test\`, \`e2e.owner+…\`) clip — deliberately, via line-clamp. The text-clip assertion recognizes \`truncate\` and \`data-allow-scroll\` as intentional-clamping markers but not \`line-clamp-*\`. Not #3756-shaped and NOT covered by the #3885 exclusion (text-clip is deliberately not allowlisted there). Question to answer: should text-clip treat \`line-clamp-*\` as intentional (like \`truncate\`), or should these spans carry an explicit marker?

2. **Mobile "Toggle Sidebar" nav-Sheet overlap remnants** (mobile-iphone13/mobile-pixel5 walker rows): 12 occurrences in BOTH nightlies — pre-existing background, unchanged by #3885. The FAB-involved instances are filed under #3889; this issue covers whatever remains after #3889 lands (sheet content vs page content at the sheet's edge). Re-measure after #3889 before deciding the rest is real.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Tablet footer-span text-clip: either \`line-clamp-*\` recognized as intentional clamping in \`assert-no-layout-bugs.ts\` (with the same anti-silencing discipline as \`truncate\`), or the spans marked explicitly — with the decision recorded
- [ ] Mobile nav-Sheet overlap rows re-measured after #3889 merges; anything still failing is itemized here with per-finding verdicts (real bug → own issue; artifact → assertion-level fix)

Refs: #3885, #3889, #3756, #3360, tracker #3126

title: L3 Overlay walker: dashboard Notifications popover overlaps nav on mobile-iphone13
body:
## Finding

Nightly run 32305107279 (2026-08-19, `E2E tests`, post-#3629): `L3: Overlay walker › dashboard: every overlay renders without layout bugs` fails on `mobile-iphone13`:

```
Layout bugs on "dashboard overlay (popover-trigger): Notifications" (1 total finding)
```

## Likely the same bug class as #3219, recurring on a different device/route

#3219 (closed 2026-08-12) fixed the identical shape — `NotificationBell`'s Popover not anchored to the true header edge, panel narrower than the full-bleed mobile buttons underneath — for the `mobile-pixel5` / `meetings list` combination (`STATE_RECIPES_WALKER_QUARANTINE`'s `state-recipes-meetings-overlay-walker@mobile-pixel5` entry, now removed as fixed — see #3631). Corroborating: today's run shows **no** mobile-pixel5 finding, but **does** show this new mobile-iphone13/dashboard one. Either the #3219 fix didn't fully generalize across devices/routes, or this is an independent recurrence of the same popover-anchoring pattern.

## Suggested next step

Reproduce against current `main` at `mobile-iphone13` (`/dashboard`, open the Notifications popover) and compare against #3219's fix in `NotificationBell` — check whether the same anchoring/responsive-width treatment needs to extend to the dashboard route's header layout, or whether iPhone13's viewport (390×844) hits a boundary the pixel5 fix (393×851) didn't cover.

## Provenance

Nightly run 32305107279 (2026-08-19). Filed as part of #3497's nightly triage, replacing the now-resolved `STATE_RECIPES_WALKER_QUARANTINE` entry that cited closed #3219 for the pixel5/meetings variant of this same bug shape.

title: docs(api): eight API resource families have no public documentation on any surviving surface
body:
## Problem

Eight resource families have **no** public documentation anywhere in the repo, and no entry in the OpenAPI spec:

`action-items`, `attachments`, `audit-log`, `fx-rates`, `invites`, `notifications`, `proposed-slots` — plus the API `contributing.md` guide and the runnable `examples/` (curl scripts, `typescript/listBoards.ts`, `smoke-test.sh`).

## How this surfaced

#3438 decommissioned the legacy VitePress site under `main/docs/api/`. Those eight resource pages (~5,600 words) lived only there. They were **not** migrated when the fumadocs port happened (`feat(docs): port all content into fresh Fumadocs v16 template`, 2026-03-29) — the port deliberately kept only the seven resources that actually shipped in the v1 public API (`me`, `boards`, `members`, `meetings`, `documents`, `reports`, `dashboards`).

**This is a pre-existing gap, not a regression from #3438.** Two independent facts confirm nothing user-visible was lost when the directory was deleted:

1. **The VitePress site never rendered publicly.** `gh api repos/imboard-ai/imboard-monorepo/pages` returns 404 — GitHub Pages was never enabled for this repo, so `docs.yml`'s deploy job failed on every push to `main` from the day it shipped (2026-04-16). No reader ever saw these pages.
2. **The endpoints they describe are not in the public v1 surface.** Neither OpenAPI spec copy had a path for any of them, and they are absent from the v1 route registry (`main/packages/backend/src/api/v1/registry/routes/`). Several exist only as legacy `/api/board/...` routes.

The deleted content is recoverable from git history at `main/docs/api/resources/` (parent of the #3438 merge commit).

## The real question to answer

Not "restore the markdown" — the pages documented an aspirational API surface from the March 2026 docs skeleton (#536) that never matched what shipped. The decision is:

- [ ] For each of the eight, decide whether the endpoints are **part of the supported public API**.
- [ ] If yes → add the paths to `main/packages/docs/content/openapi.yaml` (now the single source of truth) and write the corresponding `.mdx` under `main/packages/docs/content/docs/resources/`, adding each to that directory's `meta.json`.
- [ ] If no → they are internal/legacy surfaces and the correct outcome is to leave them undocumented. Record that so this does not get re-litigated.

Worth noting `packages/docs/content/docs/api-reference/index.mdx` hand-maintains an "Endpoints Overview" table that must stay in sync with whatever is decided.

## Also worth folding in

`examples/smoke-test.sh` and the curl/TypeScript examples were runnable API examples with no fumadocs equivalent. If the public API is meant to be self-serve, a working quickstart example is worth more than prose.

---
Filed as a merge guardrail for #3438 so the gap is tracked rather than silently absorbed by the deletion.

title: fix(backend): `rateLimitTier` on every v1 route is decorative — no middleware reads it
body:
**Found during the #3386 review. Repo-wide, not specific to that PR.**

## What happens

Every route in `packages/backend/src/api/v1/registry/routes/*.routes.ts` declares `rateLimitTier: 'none' | 'standard' | 'strict'`. **Nothing reads it.**

`register.ts` pushes `publicApiRateLimiter` unconditionally, with no tier argument:

```ts
chain.push(publicApiCorsMiddleware);
chain.push(publicApiRateLimiter);
```

A repo-wide grep finds `rateLimitTier` only in `registry/types.ts` (the type), a doc comment in `routes.ts`, and test fixtures. So a route marked `'strict'` gets the **identical** budget as one marked `'none'`.

## Why it matters

349 routes carry a field that reads as a security control and is not one. Concretely, the two most expensive surfaces in the registry are both declared `'strict'` and are not rate-limited any differently from a plain GET:

- `send_investor_update` — one call fans out N investor emails
- `search_shortlist` / `refresh_shortlist` — LLM-scored searches

Worse, for JWT callers the limiter keys on **IP** (`apiv1:jwt:<ip>` in `publicApiRateLimit.middleware.ts`), so it neither isolates an abusing account nor survives a shared NAT.

PR2 hit exactly this need for `/u/:signedToken` and had to write a bespoke middleware (`investorUpdateShareRateLimit.middleware.ts`) rather than declare a tier — which is the tell.

## Suggested fix

Either make `register.ts` compose a per-tier limiter from the declaration (and key authenticated buckets on the user id, not the IP), or delete the field so it stops reading as a control that exists. A drift test asserting the composed chain matches the declaration would keep it honest.

## Scope note

This is the kind of finding that is cheap to fix once and impossible to notice per-PR — every route author reasonably assumes the field does something.

title: CI gate: fail the terraform plan job when the rendered boundary policy nears the 6144-byte limit
body:
Follow-up from #3397 (flagged by the convention review on PR #3402, left out of scope there).

## Problem

The managed boundary (`imboard-terraform-managed-boundary`) is capped by AWS's 6144-byte managed-policy size limit, counted on the whitespace-stripped policy JSON. This limit has already bitten once: #3369 exists solely because a #3365 apply failed with `LimitExceeded: Cannot exceed quota for PolicySize: 6144` — and the trim it forced under pressure is what stripped the canary statements and caused #3395.

Current state after #3402: **5793 / 6144 bytes (351 bytes of headroom)**. Nothing in CI measures this. The next statement added to the boundary is likely the one that breaks an apply — discovered at apply time (workstation or CI), which is the worst moment to be forced into another hasty trim.

## Proposal

Fail (or loudly warn) at plan time, where there is room to think:

- In the terraform.yml plan job (natural home: alongside the #3397 boundary guard, which already extracts the rendered boundary from `tfplan.json`), measure the proposed boundary's size the way AWS counts it:
  ```bash
  jq -r '.planned_values.root_module.resources[]
    | select(.address=="aws_iam_policy.terraform_managed_boundary")
    | .values.policy | gsub("[\\s]"; "") | length' tfplan.json
  ```
  (Note: terraform already renders the policy minified; confirm whether `gsub` is needed or `length` alone matches AWS's count — #3369/#3402 measured with whitespace stripped.)
- Two thresholds: **error ≥ 6144** (the apply will fail anyway — fail fast with a message pointing at the trim discipline in `iam-github-terraform.tf`'s header and the #3397 guard), **warning ≥ ~5900** (≤ ~250 bytes headroom — plan the next trim deliberately instead of under a failed apply).
- Cheapest implementation: a few lines appended to `scripts/terraform-boundary-guard.sh` (it already holds the parsed boundary and has the ::error/::warning plumbing), plus a couple of assertions in `scripts/tests/test-terraform-boundary-guard.sh`.

## Acceptance

- A fixture boundary over 6144 rendered bytes fails the guard with a message naming the limit and the current size.
- A fixture in the warning band passes with a visible `::warning` naming the remaining headroom.
- Current main passes clean (5793 bytes → warning band starts above it, or tune the threshold so today's state is green).
- Any trim made to fit MUST be checked against capped roles' runtime actions — which the #3397 guard now enforces automatically; the size gate's error text should say so, so the #3369→#3395 sequence (trim under pressure → silent runtime strip) cannot repeat.

Refs: #2782 (boundary), #3369 (the LimitExceeded trim), #3395 (what the trim broke), #3397/#3402 (the guard this extends).

title: chore(dossier): wire ai-dossier cap run into implement-issue / full-cycle-issue for the steps #3958's manifest covers
body:
## Context
#3958 seeded `.dossier/automation/manifest.yaml` with 7 `active` capabilities (`dependencies.install`, `lint.run`, `typecheck.run`, `test.full`, `test.focused`, `environment.start`/`environment.stop`) and verified each via direct `ai-dossier cap run <id>` calls (recorded in `~/.dossier/caps.jsonl`). That satisfies AC1-AC4 of #3958.

AC5 of #3958 ("One full-cycle run on a real issue observed using the capabilities … with no fallback to reasoning for the covered steps") could NOT be satisfied within that issue's scope: it was an explicit non-goal ("generic dossier changes; anything beyond this repo's manifest"). Confirmed via grep during #3958's review: `ai-dossier cap` / `cap run` appears zero times in `imboard-ai/git/implement-issue` or `imboard-ai/git/full-cycle-issue`. Only `imboard-ai/git/slot-cycle` already probes for `cap run test.focused` when present (per #3958's own issue body).

## Scope
- `implement-issue` — for the steps the manifest already declares `active` (lint, typecheck, test, dependency install, env start/stop), check `ai-dossier cap list --json` first; if the relevant capability exists and is `active`, call `ai-dossier cap run <id>` instead of reasoning through the equivalent prose steps. Fall back to the existing prose path when the manifest doesn't exist or the capability isn't `active` (this must stay portable to repos with no manifest at all).
- `full-cycle-issue` (or whichever sub-dossier owns the CI-parity check) — same treatment for `lint.run`/`typecheck.run` where applicable.
- Non-goal (still, in this follow-up too): do NOT wire `worktree.prepare`/`worktree.cleanup` — those stay `shadow` in imboard-monorepo's manifest per #3958 AC2 until 5 clean shadow agreements, which is a separate, not-yet-built automation-miner mechanism.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `implement-issue` calls `ai-dossier cap run <id>` for at least `lint.run`/`typecheck.run`/`test.focused` when the target repo's manifest declares them `active`, with a prose fallback when it doesn't
- [ ] One real full-cycle run on an imboard-monorepo issue shows the corresponding `cap run` invocations in `~/.dossier/caps.jsonl` with timestamps inside that run's window, and no reasoning-driven equivalent for the same covered steps
- [ ] This satisfies #3958's AC5 retroactively — link back to it in the PR

## Test strategy
One full-cycle-issue run against a real, small imboard-monorepo issue; inspect `caps.jsonl` for the run's window.

Related: #3958

title: bug(documents): create and rename accept duplicate titles per board — the de-dup helper exists but is scoped to AI-derived titles only (BUG_059)
body:
# bug(documents): create and rename accept duplicate titles per board — the de-dup helper exists but is scoped to AI-derived titles only (BUG_059)

## Provenance

Manual QA by a tester, 27-08-2026, production app.imboard.ai. [Bug sheet](https://example.invalid/redacted-bug-sheet row **BUG_059** (Medium). Evidence: screenshot https://example.invalid/redacted-screenshot (readable; OCR-verified on the documents list — same-titled rows).

## Tester's evidence (verbatim)

"Users are able to create multiple documents with the same name, which can cause confusion when identifying or managing documents."

## Where it lives

Files touched: packages/backend/src/controllers/documentController.ts (ctrlCreateDocument :118-210, ctrlUpdateDocument :719-803), packages/backend/src/models/document.model.ts, packages/frontend/src/app/dashboard/documents/[documentId]/document-details-page.tsx (rename dialog client hint)

## Root cause

CONFIRMED — no uniqueness constraint anywhere on the title path:

- Schema: `title` has required/maxlength/trim only (`document.schema.ts:34-39`); indexes are compound non-unique (`document.model.ts:11-16`) — no `{boardId, title}` unique index.
- Create (`:144-163` title resolution → `:169` create) and rename (`:785` findByIdAndUpdate) perform no duplicate lookup; route validators check string/whitespace/length only.
- Ironic near-miss: `ensureUniqueTitleForBoard` exists (`titleDerivationService.ts:166-184`) — appends a date qualifier on collision — but is called only for **AI-derived** titles (`:45`, `:196`). Filename-derived and user-typed titles bypass it entirely, so uploading the same file twice yields identical titles (the exact screenshot symptom).
- Codebase precedent supports **reject**: boards reject duplicate names at the service level (`isBoardNameTaken`, `boardController.ts:62-68`, enforced `:105-108` and `:389-394`) with the documented caveat "service check, not an index".
- No slugs exist (URLs are id-based), so this is disambiguation/UX, not routing collision.

## Detection gap

`document.test.ts` runs 11 active tests (happy-path + visibility) — no uniqueness case. The route-coverage ratchet has named these routes uncovered (advisory) every PR. Add the duplicate-title case (2nd create → 409) here.

## Decision

**LOCKED 2026-09-01** — see the decision comment below: **reject** duplicate titles (active docs, same board, case-insensitive after trim) with a 409 that carries a suggested free `<title> (n)`; the dialogs render it inline with a one-click **Use "…"** control. AI-derived titles keep the silent suffix. The acceptance criteria in that comment supersede any earlier draft.

## Explicitly out of scope

- A unique Mongo index (fails to build on existing dup data; needs a cleanup migration and collation decision — separate hardening if wanted).
- Cross-board uniqueness.
- A "Replace" option (no document versioning exists).

## Readiness

**Verdict: READY** — decision locked; implementation is fully specified in the decision comment.

title: feat(audit): extend AuditLog with append-only meeting and action-item change history
body:
# Goal hypothesis

If every meeting lifecycle/content mutation and action-item mutation appends a typed entry to the existing `AuditLog`, governance users can trust completed/finalized meeting records and reconstruct every authorized change without relying on mutable `updatedBy` fields or operational logs.

## Existing foundation

Imboard already has an established append-only `AuditLog` system: typed action/detail contracts in `@imboard/shared-types`, a Mongo audit model, a board-scoped audit retrieval endpoint, and audit writers for several domains. The strongest implementation precedent is `boardUserUnregisteredAudit.service.ts`, which creates snapshots and field-level diffs.

The gap is specific: ordinary meeting edits, meeting lifecycle/status transitions, and action-item mutations currently do not emit `AuditLog` entries. Guest meeting slot/vote audit actions exist, but they describe anonymous guest activity and must not be repurposed for authenticated governance history.

Parent UX/governance decision: #3861.

## Scope

Extend the existing `AuditLog` action catalog, validation, and write infrastructure for:

- Meeting content mutations: details, agenda, minutes, scheduling fields, and other mutable meeting-record fields.
- Meeting lifecycle transitions, including completed/finalized transitions and any reopen path.
- Action-item create, update, status mutation, and deletion/soft deletion, across legacy, v1, MCP, and post-meeting write paths.

Each event must include at least: actor identity, timestamp, action/entity type, entity and parent-meeting identifiers, and an immutable before/after snapshot or field-level diff sufficient to reconstruct the change.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Extend the shared `AuditLog` action catalog and deny-by-default detail schemas with typed meeting and action-item mutation events; do not introduce a parallel audit store or overload guest-vote actions.
- [ ] Use a reusable meeting/action-item audit service patterned on the existing unregistered-member audit service.
- [ ] Audit writes occur atomically with the corresponding domain mutation, or the implementation documents and tests its explicit consistency boundary. Audit failure must not silently permit an unrecorded authorized governance mutation.
- [ ] All listed meeting and action-item write paths emit events, including direct action-item endpoints that do not flow through meeting PUT/PATCH.
- [ ] Events capture actor, timestamp, action/entity, parent meeting, target entity, and before/after values or an equivalent field-level diff.
- [ ] Integration tests prove emitted history for representative legacy and v1/MCP paths, lifecycle/reopen behavior, and action-item mutations.
- [ ] Authorization failures and rejected locked-record writes do not create misleading success audit events; if attempted-change records are required, distinguish them explicitly.
- [ ] The existing board audit retrieval returns history in an explicit, documented chronological order.
- [ ] No existing audit consumer regresses; `pnpm run hygiene` and `bash scripts/ci-parity.sh` pass.

## Explicitly out of scope

- A new end-user audit-history viewer, unless required to validate a backend retrieval contract.
- Changing the #3861 decision that action items remain editable after a meeting is completed/finalized.
